newsitem.title: JAPAN: Key TIFFE Euroyen futures end at day low in Tokyo.
newsitem.headline: Key TIFFE Euroyen futures end at day low in Tokyo.

text.p: The key September three-month Euroyen contract ended at the day's low on Tuesday in response to a price retreat in the yen bond market after its recent rally, traders said.

"Sentiment was depressed a bit by a small retreat by the JGBs, which induced corrective selling in the Euroyen," said a city bank trader. But he added that the new key September is likely to stay in a range of 99.18-99.28 for the time being.

The government's Economic Planning Agency (EPA) said gross domestic product (GDP) -- a key gauge of the economy's health -- rose a real 0.1 percent in the July-September period from the previous quarter.

Traders said the GDP data, which was announced after the day session closed, was roughly in line with earlier market forecasts, but created an atmosphere which discouraged fresh buying in the Euroyen market.
In the interest rate swap (IRS) market, many traders became interested in paying fixed interest rates, though the market was thin due to the relative lack of IRS receivers.
